title: Midwifery injections: oxytocin units, vitamin K for the newborn, pethidine
blurb: Calculate oxytocin, vitamin K, pethidine and magnesium sulfate injection volumes from the label, including tiny newborn volumes.
question: A woman in labour is prescribed pethidine 75 mg by intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 100 mg in 2 mL. What volume should be drawn up?

teach.h: One formula across the birth unit
teach.body: Formal rule: volume = (dose prescribed ÷ dose in stock) × stock volume, with both doses in the same unit (units, mg or micrograms). Plain English: oxytocin in units, vitamin K in mg and pethidine in mg all use want ÷ have × volume. The midwifery Part A paper used pethidine, oxytocin units and newborn doses, so expect at least one of these.
teach.cite: Pearson VUE NMC practice paper (midwife, Part A)

teach.h: Common birth-unit labels (always given in the stem)
head: Medicine
Example label
Per mL
teach.caption: NICE NG235: oxytocin 10 units IM, or 5 units by slow IV injection, in the third stage.

teach.h: Worked example: Grace on the labour ward
teach.body: Grace Adeyemi, 29, is in established labour and is prescribed pethidine 75 mg IM. The ampoule reads 100 mg in 2 mL. Volume = 75 ÷ 100 × 2 = 1.5 mL. Sense-check: 100 mg in 2 mL is 50 mg per mL, and 75 mg is one and a half lots of 50 mg. Type 1.5 mL.

rows.label: Correct: 0.4 mg from 2 mg in 0.2 mL

teach.caption: The ampoule volume is 0.2 mL, not 1 mL. That final multiply is easy to miss.

teach.text: Treating "2 mg in 0.2 mL" as 2 mg in 1 mL. The strength is 10 mg per mL, so 1 mg is 0.1 mL. Forgetting the 0.2 mL makes a newborn's volume five times too big.

teach.body: Oxytocin is prescribed in units and labelled units per mL. 5 units from 10 units in 1 mL is 0.5 mL, not 5 mL. Oxytocin with ergometrine (5 units and 500 micrograms in 1 mL) contains two drugs, so read which one the question asks about. 500 micrograms of ergometrine is 0.5 mg.

items: Oxytocin: units ÷ units per mL; units are not mL.
Vitamin K 2 mg in 0.2 mL: multiply by 0.2, not by 1.
Pethidine 100 mg in 2 mL is 50 mg per mL.
Magnesium sulfate 50% = 500 mg in 1 mL: convert g to mg first.
Convert a baby's weight from g to kg before any per-kg dose.

summary: You can now calculate the injection volumes a midwife draws up most often: oxytocin in units, vitamin K for the newborn, pethidine and magnesium sulfate. You can also handle the 0.2 mL vitamin K ampoule and weights in grams without a slip.

A.q: A woman in labour is prescribed pethidine 75 mg by intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 100 mg in 2 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This forgets the 2 mL stock volume (0.75 rounds to 0.8).
whyNot.2: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.3: This reads the label as 10 mg per mL, a tenfold error.

A.q: A preterm baby is prescribed phytomenadione (vitamin K) 0.4 mg by intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 2 mg in 0.2 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: This forgets the 0.2 mL ampoule volume.
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This reads 0.4 mg as 4 mg, a tenfold error.

A.q: Oxytocin with ergometrine injection contains oxytocin 5 units and ergometrine 500 micrograms in 1 mL. How many mg of ergometrine are in 1 mL? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.1: This divides by 100, a tenfold error.
whyNot.2: This divides by 10,000, a tenfold error the other way.
whyNot.3: This gives the micrograms figure but labels it mg.

B.q: A woman in labour is prescribed pethidine 75 mg by intramuscular injection. The ampoules available each contain 50 mg in 1 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction (0.67 rounds to 0.7).
whyNot.1: This treats the label as 50 mg in 2 mL.
whyNot.3: This uses 100 mg per mL, not the 50 mg in 1 mL on the label (0.75 rounds to 0.8).

B.q: A newborn baby is prescribed phytomenadione (vitamin K) 2 mg by mouth. The ampoule label reads 2 mg in 0.2 mL. What volume should be given? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.1: This uses a 1 mL stock volume instead of 0.2 mL.
whyNot.2: This reads the ampoule as 0.02 mL, a tenfold error.
whyNot.3: This is the volume for a 1 mg dose; the prescription is 2 mg.

B.q: A woman is prescribed oxytocin 10 units by intramuscular injection. The ampoules available each contain oxytocin 5 units in 1 mL. How many ampoules are needed?

whyNot.0: One ampoule holds 5 units, half the dose.
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.
whyNot.2: This multiplies the dose by the strength.

C.q: A preterm baby weighing 2350 g is prescribed phytomenadione (vitamin K) 400 micrograms/kg by intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 2 mg in 0.2 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.
C.why: Weight = 2.35 kg. Dose = 400 × 2.35 = 940 micrograms = 0.94 mg. Volume = 0.94 ÷ 2 × 0.2 = 0.094, which is 0.09 mL to two decimal places.

whyNot.0: This uses 2 mL for the ampoule volume instead of 0.2 mL.
whyNot.1: This forgets the 0.2 mL ampoule volume.
whyNot.3: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.

C.q: A woman in labour is given pethidine 100 mg by intramuscular injection, then a further 50 mg three hours later. The ampoule label reads 100 mg in 2 mL. What total volume of pethidine has she received? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This forgets the 2 mL stock volume.
whyNot.2: This counts only the first dose.
whyNot.3: This uses 50 mg per mL and then doubles again.

C.q: A woman with severe pre-eclampsia is prescribed a loading dose of magnesium sulfate 4 g by intravenous injection over 5 to 15 minutes. The ampoule label reads magnesium sulfate 50%, 500 mg in 1 mL. What volume of the 50% solution should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit.
C.why: Convert: 4 g = 4000 mg. Volume = 4000 ÷ 500 × 1 = 8 mL. The 4 g loading dose over 5 to 15 minutes, then 1 g per hour, is the Collaborative Eclampsia Trial regimen in NICE NG133 rec 1.8.4.

whyNot.1: This divides 4 g by 500 mg without converting g to mg (0.008).
whyNot.2: This reads 50% as 50 mg in 1 mL; 50% is 50 g in 100 mL, which is 500 mg in 1 mL.
whyNot.3: This is have ÷ want (500 ÷ 4000), the inverted fraction.

reteach.title: Check the stock volume
reteach.question: Vitamin K 1 mg is prescribed and the ampoule says 2 mg in 0.2 mL. What volume?

blocks.body: 1 ÷ 2 × 0.2 = 0.1 mL. The last number is the volume the label gives (0.2 mL), not 1 mL.

blocks.text: Stopping at 0.5 and drawing up 0.5 mL: five times the prescribed dose for a newborn.

explain.body: Units = volume × units per mL. 0.5 mL of 10 units in 1 mL = 5 units.

test.q: An oxytocin ampoule contains 10 units in 1 mL. How many units of oxytocin are in 0.5 mL?

whyNot.1: This writes the volume as if it were the units.
whyNot.3: This uses 100 units per mL, a tenfold error.

test.q: An ampoule of phytomenadione (vitamin K) contains 2 mg in 0.2 mL. How many mg are in 0.1 mL? Please use the correct unit.
test.why: 0.1 mL is half of 0.2 mL, so it holds half of 2 mg: 1 mg.

whyNot.1: This treats the label as 2 mg in 1 mL.
whyNot.3: This uses 100 mg per mL, a tenfold error.

explain.body: 50 mg in each mL. 50 mg is 1 mL; 100 mg is 2 mL; 75 mg is 1.5 mL.

test.q: A woman is prescribed pethidine 50 mg by intramuscular injection. The ampoule label reads 100 mg in 2 mL. What volume should be drawn up? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This forgets the 2 mL stock volume.
whyNot.1: This is have ÷ want, the inverted fraction.

explain.h: Grams to kg, then the dose

test.q: A baby weighs 2500 g and is prescribed a medicine 0.4 mg/kg. What dose should be given? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This uses the weight in grams as if it were kg.
whyNot.2: This converts 2500 g to 0.25 kg, a tenfold error.
